items.title: Snooky Young and Gerald Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: Wendell Culley and myself was the trumpet section. Henry Coker, Al Grey and Benny Powell were the trombone section. And the reeds was Marshall Royal, baritone was Charlie Fowlkes, Frank Wess, Frank Foster, and Billy Mitchell.

ctx.x: What was the first fast company you came back into?

Count Basie. And that was when he was the hottest. I mean his next trip around, “The Comeback.” Joe Williams was in the band then, you know? And oh, that was, Thad Jones, Joe Newman, Wendell Culley and myself was the trumpet section. Henry Coker, Al Grey and Benny Powell were the trombone section. And the reeds was Marshall Royal, baritone was Charlie Fowlkes, Frank Wess, Frank Foster, and Billy Mitchell. Billy Mitchell. And the rhythm section was of course Freddie Green, Jo Jones, Eddie Jones and Sonny Payne and…

items.title: Young Snooky — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Marshall Royal used to conduct the band a lot.

ctx.x: He hired someone else to help lead the band, maybe not artistically, but maybe like a…you said there was somebody else who helped Count Basie run the band?
No, Marshall Royal used to conduct the band a lot.
So he was the straw boss for the Basie band?
